column1: # Curated packet field names. HAND-MAINTAINED -- name_fields.py reads this and
# never writes it.
# These outrank everything the generator infers, because they came from
# rebuilding captured replies byte-for-byte rather than from a heuristic. They
# are also the only source for client->server packets: the client parses what
# it receives and builds what it sends, so there is no reader handler to
# decompile for any CZ_/CB_ opcode (docs/08-struct-extraction.md).
# columns:  opcode  offset  type  name  fmt  source
#   offset  from the start of the packet, header included -- the same base the
#           hex panel counts from. Client packets carry a 22-byte header, not
#           10, so their body offsets start at 0x16 (docs/07).
#   type    u8 u16 u32 u64 i8 i16 i32 i64 f32 f64  |  f32[N] str[N] bytes[N]
#           N = 0 means "to the end of the packet", which is how a trailing
#           NUL-terminated text field is written (ZC_CHAT, CZ_CHAT).
#   fmt     how the viewer renders the value, blank for plain:
#             hex   0x0000339CC -- handles, colours, ids read as hex
#             bool  a flag the protocol only ever sets to 0 or 1
#             time  a float on the server clock (docs/05)
#             text  NUL-terminated, show as a string
#             ip    u32 formatted %d.%d.%d.%d from its bytes (docs/09)
#   source  where the name came from; shown in the pane's origin column
# The client packets carry no handle: the zone knows who is asking. Every echo
# inserts it at +0x0A and passes the same floats straight back.
